text:
Did you hear about how Trump has started mailing out so-called ACA Refund Checks? After driving up health care costs, this is a slap in the face to all of us. And the timing… well the timing speaks for itself.

Here’s what you need to know:

First, Trump and his Rubber Stamp Republicans in Washington let ACA tax credits expire last year, driving up health care costs for millions of Americans. Health care premiums jumped by over $700 per year, per person, with families often seeing annual premium increases in the thousands.

As a result, over 2 million people have lost ACA coverage, unable to afford higher prices. In Ohio, we had the largest coverage drop, by percentage, in the country, with over 100,000 people losing coverage.

What’s worse? House Democrats forced a vote to extend these credits, which passed, but the President blocked the extension.

Now, just weeks before an election, Trump is mailing out $500 checks with a propaganda letter littered with lies. He claims these are rebates from excess fees.

But everyone is receiving the same “rebate” amount. How did they pick who got rebates? Well according to Reuters, 71% of these checks are going to just 13 states, and most of them are now states with the most competitive races, including Ohio.

Here’s the kicker: while more than 2 million Americans have lost their ACA plans and more than 20 million Americans have been enrolled in ACA plans in the past, Trump is mailing these checks to just a small number of people – less than one million.

None of this adds up. Instead of lowering premiums, restoring affordable coverage, or helping families get back on a plan they can afford, Trump is sending out checks that don’t begin to cover the costs he’s helped create.

In other words, it’s a failed PR stunt … one that is more than a day late and a dollar short.

text:
Welcome home, USS Abraham Lincoln. 

Today San Diego gets its Marines and Sailors back, and I could not be happier for them and for the families who have waited so long for this day.

Those families spent months raising the alarm about food shortages, broken plumbing, contaminated water and sailors going overboard. Pete Hegseth brushed them off as fake news.

Now Hegseth claims those calling out the conditions on the Lincoln are trying to turn it "into some sort of a symbol, a symbol of dysfunction or a symbol of low morale or a symbol of a failed mission." Wrong. The only symbol on that ship is courage. 

Our questions are for him and those in charge.

And it goes far beyond the conditions on the ship. What is the mission? How will success be measured?

Mark Esper, who served as Defense Secretary in President Trump's first term, now says this war could run well into 2027 and may be handed to the next administration in 2029. He also warns that our focus on the Middle East is pulling attention from China, which he calls our greatest adversary and which has carried out the largest military buildup in history.

Our service members deserve a clear mission, an honest accounting, and a plan that keeps America strong where it matters most. That starts at the top.

We must keep demanding answers.
https://t.co/KR2kdo6yHF

If that was true, the military would have come to me and my colleagues on the Appropriations Committee to request those funds. That request doesn’t exist.

First the observation deck on top of the arch was for tourists. Then it was for the military. Now it’s suddenly a full-blown military complex to house drones, snipers, and ammunition.

No one wants this absurd display of vanity next to Arlington National Cemetery. Not our veterans, not their families, not the American people.

text:
I could not be happier to welcome the Marines and Sailors of the USS Abraham Lincoln home to San Diego today after an extraordinarily long, demanding, and difficult deployment.
 
These heroes have done everything their country asked of them and more, and they have earned this homecoming. But their return cannot be the end of this story. 
 
What happened aboard the Lincoln cannot ever be allowed to happen again.
 
This Administration owes these families answers: answers to conditions aboard the ship and what will be done differently going forward. 
 
For months, Marines and Sailors sounded the alarm about conditions aboard the ship, inadequate support, and the mental health toll this deployment was taking on those serving onboard. Their families begged for help and were repeatedly ignored.
 
And when those families were forced to turn to the press just to be heard, Pete Hegseth responded by telling the world the reports were fake news.
 
That is beyond unacceptable. It's a betrayal of the men and women who put everything on the line for this country. 
 
Secretary Hegseth now wants to suggest that holding him accountable somehow diminishes the service of the Lincoln’s crew.
 
The opposite is true. Honoring them means telling the truth about what they went through. It means finding out why their warnings were ignored, who failed them, and what is going to change before another crew is put through the same thing.
 
I need firm assurances from this Administration that the crews now carrying out these and future missions will never be subjected to the same failures.
 
Our Marines and Sailors upheld their duty to this country, and the people entrusted with leading them must be held to theirs.

text:
321 days.

That's how long the USS Abraham Lincoln and its thousands of servicemembers have been away from their families and their home port of San Diego.

And today, for the first time in 10 months, they return home. They hug loved ones. They sleep out of harm's way.

In the time these men and women were deployed as the tip of the spear in the Iran war, they worked tirelessly. And that service took a heavy toll – a price we have come to know through harrowing stories shared by family members and even the military's own leadership. The crew of the Abraham Lincoln has faced long and grueling shifts, diminished supplies and even mental health crises. Those burdens of such a long deployment have been shouldered by the crew and their families back in San Diego.

As we welcome them home today, and we hear more of those stories of hardship and sacrifice, I hope these heavy burdens resonate through the halls of the White House and the Pentagon. With no clear objective and no measurable progress, this war must end. Not just for the sake of the higher costs this war has imposed on the American people, but for the sake of those servicemembers who have paid an even higher price. Those who have been asked to miss holidays, birthdays, births and weddings for nearly a year in order to sustain this war of choice.

Only last week, the USS Theodore Roosevelt and its carrier strike group left San Diego. All signs point to its crew being relief for a beleaguered force still deployed in the Middle East. I hope for the sake of our sailors, Marines, soldiers, guardians and airmen that this new deployment of Californians does not repeat the hardships of the Abraham Lincoln.⁩⁩

text:
Statement on Trump Suspending Microsoft from the PERM Program:

This is a crucial issue for me as the top Democrat on the Immigration Subcommittee, the only member of Congress to have actually had an H-1B visa, and the Representative for tens of thousands of Microsoft workers. The administration has been consistently working to take away legal pathways for immigrants to contribute their talents to our country, and this is yet another of those attacks.

The PERM program is the first step toward an employment-based green card for countless workers who want to contribute to this country, and it lays out a clear process with steps to ensure that this is a net benefit to our economy and does not harm American jobs. Our economy, our communities, and our families depend on immigrants in many sectors, including the tech sector, and heavy-handed attacks like this only hurt efforts to build a strong, stable, and diverse base of workers who have legal pathways to come and be in the United States while also protecting U.S. workers from unscrupulous employers.

You don’t fix a broken immigration system by taking a hammer to legal immigration. Microsoft has been a leader in advocating for comprehensive immigration reforms that modernize an antiquated immigration system and provide more — not fewer — legal pathways for immigrants from all over the world to work here and be with their families. Targeting Microsoft or the PERM program in this way simply undermines legal immigration and weakens America’s ability to innovate.

text:
Welcome home to the sailors of the USS Abraham Lincoln after 265 uninterrupted days at sea.

These sailors spent months away from their families while carrying out a demanding mission overseas. Today, they are finally returning home to spouses, children, parents, and loved ones who have been waiting a long time for this day.

Extended deployments ask a great deal of our service members and their families, and they deserve our gratitude and support when they return home.

To the entire USS Abraham Lincoln crew, and especially any Texans serving aboard, welcome home. I hope you get some well-earned time with your families and loved ones.

As a member of the House Defense Appropriations Subcommittee, I’m committed to making sure our service members, veterans, and military families have the support they have earned.

https://t.co/mrlDwCk1Ma

text:
Read more about this in The Hill via @NateWeixel: 

"The Trump administration violated federal law by withholding tens of millions of dollars in research grant funding Congress had appropriated for the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)...

"The AHRQ is a relatively small federal agency dedicated to making healthcare safer, more affordable and more effective and is estimated to have funded research that’s saved thousands of lives and billions of dollars over the past 27 years.

"But the agency’s failure to spend appropriated dollars continues.

"Congress allocated about $345 million for the AHRQ this year, but the agency in July told researchers it was halting nearly every grant that previously had been awarded.

"Last month, the White House told Congress it intended to claw back $28 million of AHRQ funding as part of a broader move to cancel nearly $1 billion in federal funding across various agencies."

https://t.co/0iKifjzB6m

Her speech speaks to a broader frustration among people who placed their hopes in electoral politics as a vehicle for advancing Palestinian liberation. For some, the experience hasn’t strengthened their faith in political institutions. It has deepened their distrust.
